_meta.note: Curated subset of the Gitleaks default rule set, hand-written from the well-known default rules (AWS, GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Stripe, private keys, generic assignments). No live fetch of the Gitleaks config was available in this sandbox, so the patterns below were written from the known default rule set and are documented as such; no Gitleaks code is used — patterns only, matched by this engine. Attribution: Gitleaks (github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks), MIT license.

rules.fix: Rotate the key in AWS IAM, remove it from the repo, and move it to a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: AWS access key

rules.description: AWS secret access key assignment (40-char base64).
rules.fix: Rotate the key in AWS IAM, remove it from the repo, and move it to a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: AWS secret key

rules.description: GitHub personal access token (classic ghp_ or fine-grained github_pat_).
rules.fix: Revoke the token at github.com/settings/tokens, remove it from the repo, and use a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: GitHub personal access token

rules.fix: Revoke the token in GitLab, remove it from the repo, and use a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: GitLab personal access token

rules.fix: Revoke the token in Slack, remove it from the repo, and use a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: Slack API token

rules.fix: Delete the webhook in Slack, remove the URL from the repo, and use a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: Slack webhook URL

rules.description: Stripe secret or restricted live/test key.
rules.fix: Roll the key in the Stripe dashboard, remove it from the repo, and use a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: Stripe secret key

rules.description: Private key block (RSA, EC, DSA, OpenSSH, PGP, encrypted).
rules.fix: Remove the key from the repo, revoke/replace it everywhere it was used, and store it in a secret manager. Never commit private keys.
rules.name: Private key

rules.fix: Treat it as compromised if it was live: revoke/rotate it, remove it from the repo, and use a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: JSON Web Token

rules.fix: Revoke the token at npmjs.com, remove it from the repo, and use a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: npm access token

rules.fix: Delete the key in SendGrid, remove it from the repo, and use a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: SendGrid API key

rules.description: Generic API-key assignment (key-like variable holding a long token). Skips lines already flagged by a specific rule, and skips obvious placeholders.
rules.fix: Remove the key from the repo and move it to a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: Generic API key

rules.description: Generic password/secret assignment. Skips lines already flagged by a specific rule, and skips obvious placeholders.
rules.fix: Remove the credential from the repo, rotate it, and move it to a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: Generic password or secret

rules.fix: Regenerate the key in the Azure portal, remove it from the repo, and use a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: Azure storage account key

rules.fix: Delete the key in Google Cloud Console, remove it from the repo, and use a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: Google API key

rules.fix: Delete the key in Google Cloud Console, remove the file from the repo, and use a secret manager or workload identity.
rules.name: GCP service account key

rules.fix: Delete the key in the Twilio console, remove it from the repo, and use a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: Twilio API key

rules.description: OpenAI API key (sk-proj-… or legacy sk- + 48 chars).
rules.fix: Revoke the key at platform.openai.com, remove it from the repo, and use a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: OpenAI API key

rules.description: Database connection string with embedded credentials (postgres/mysql/mongodb URI with user:password@host).
rules.fix: Rotate the database credentials, remove the URI from the repo, and pass the connection string via a secret manager or environment variable.
rules.name: Database connection string
